Recorded as a Gate 6 finding against this run (CO-7): the ledger should have been created at Step 0 and appended per pass. Two consequences a reviewer must weigh. (1) Rows are reconstructed, not captured live, so a finding raised and silently dropped without reaching a commit message would not appear here - absence is weaker evidence in this fragment than in one written live. (2) The six passes ran with a two-dot 'origin/dev..HEAD' range in the agent prompts while the branch was 5 commits behind dev, so dev-ahead work rendered to the agents as removals; two agents caught it, earlier ones may have been misled. The branch has since been rebased onto b061cd74, so the range above is the corrected three-dot form and no longer reproduces what those agents saw. (3) Every `reporter` value names a governance subagent of the change author's own session, and the rows were transcribed by the party under review from a record he authored. `independent_reporters` therefore measures evidence convergence between reviewers who could not see each other, NOT independent review by a second party. The README's stated purpose is retrievability by someone other than the producer, which this satisfies; reviewer independence is the human PR approval, which is external to this artefact. Read this fragment as SUPPORTING evidence of the review activity, with the commit messages as the primary contemporaneous record - not as the complete finding population for the run.

Fixed by publishing a read-only SELECT that can, and stating both limits of the route.
